claim_texts: The relationship api.oauthflow associated-with api.oauthflows understates a real composition, because the OAuthFlows container owns the flow.
api.response is related to api.components by both an aggregates and a composes relationship, which express the same meaning redundantly.
api.components has both an aggregates and a composes relationship to api.response, which are redundant and contradictory.

The relationships from api.requestbody to api.example (aggregates), api.encoding (associated-with) and api.schema (references) are indirect because these elements hang off api.mediatype, not api.requestbody.
api.oauthflows has both an aggregates and a composes relationship to api.oauthflow, which express the same meaning.
The link from api.oauthflows to api.oauthflow is listed both as 'aggregates' and as 'composes', which express the same meaning.
api.oauthflows has both aggregates and composes relationships to api.oauthflow, which are contradictory because OAuthFlow cannot exist outside OAuthFlows, so composes is correct.
The relationships api.encoding composes api.header and api.encoding references api.header are not redundant: composes is an inline header declaration while references is a $ref.
The serves relationship from api.oauthflows to api.securityscheme should be composition, since the security scheme composes OAuthFlows (and api.securityscheme already composes api.oauthflows).

The relationships from api.requestbody to api.example (aggregates), api.encoding (associated-with) and api.schema (references) are indirect because these elements hang off api.mediatype, not api.requestbody.
The 'serves' predicate from api.ratelimit to api.operation and api.pathitem inverts the usual meaning, since a rate limit restricts rather than provides functionality.
The 'governs' and 'serves' relationships from api.ratelimit to api.operation appear redundant.
The relationships api.ratelimit governs api.operation and api.ratelimit serves api.operation are redundant because both attach a rate limit to an operation, and 'governs' fits better.

The associated-with relationship from api.externaldocumentation to api.info is questionable and redundant, because OpenAPI does not allow externalDocs to attach to Info; it attaches to the root document, which already has a serves relationship.
api.mediatype has both aggregates and composes relationships to api.encoding, which are contradictory because Encoding cannot exist outside its MediaType, so only composes should remain.
The outgoing composes relationships from api.openapidocument to api.responses and api.schema contradict OpenAPI, where these live under Components or Operations rather than the root document.
The composes relationship from api.openapidocument to api.responses is wrong because a Responses map is scoped to an operation, not the document.

api.components relationships to registry entry kinds use aggregates for some kinds (callback, example, link, requestbody, response) and composes for others (header, parameter, schema, securityscheme) with no clear basis for the difference.
The relationship api.requestbody serves api.operation has odd semantics and points the wrong way; the operation should own the request body as part of its contract.

The relationships api.responses aggregates api.header, api.responses aggregates api.schema and api.responses references api.link are transitive shortcuts, because headers, schemas and links belong to individual Response objects (or MediaType), not to the Responses map.
The relationships api.operation composes api.schema and api.operation references api.schema overlap, differing only in inline versus $ref.
api.paths has duplicate aggregates and composes relationships to api.pathitem that express the same meaning.

api.paths has both an aggregates and a composes relationship to api.pathitem, which express the same meaning redundantly; composes should be kept and aggregates reserved for $ref'd components/pathItems.

api.components relationships to registry entry kinds use aggregates for some kinds (callback, example, link, requestbody, response) and composes for others (header, parameter, schema, securityscheme) with no clear basis for the difference.

The relationship api.encoding associated-with api.mediatype understates the link, because MediaType composes its encoding entries; it should be expressed as composition from MediaType (api.mediatype composes api.encoding already exists).
The relationship 'serves' from api.server to application.applicationcomponent inverts the usual dependency direction and should be reviewed.
The relationship api.server serves application.applicationcomponent has an inverted direction, since the component is exposed via the server.

The relationship api.pathitem realizes business.businessfunction is unusual because business behaviour is normally realized by the operation or an application service rather than directly by a path item.

The direct api.response to api.schema (aggregates and references) and api.response references api.example relationships are indirect in OAS 3.0, since responses reach schemas and examples only through media types or headers, making them transitive shortcuts of the mediatype/header relationships.

api.components relationships to registry entry kinds use aggregates for some kinds (callback, example, link, requestbody, response) and composes for others (header, parameter, schema, securityscheme) with no clear basis for the difference.
api.response has both aggregates and composes relationships to api.header, which express overlapping meaning; they should be distinguished (e.g. $ref-reused versus inline) or one dropped.
The relationship from api.info to api.openapidocument with predicate 'associated-with' duplicates the composes relationship from api.openapidocument to api.info.

The relationship api.info --[associated-with]--> api.openapidocument is weak and redundant, because Info cannot exist without its document and the inverse api.openapidocument composes api.info already expresses the accurate structural relation.
The outgoing 'references' relationship from api.parameter to api.operation is redundant because operation-to-parameter already exists as an aggregates relationship, and it points the opposite way.

The relationship api.parameter references api.operation is inverted, since operations contain parameters; an operation-to-parameter composes/aggregates relationship fits better (api.operation aggregates api.parameter already exists).
The aggregates and references relationships from api.response to api.schema overlap in meaning.

The direct api.response to api.schema (aggregates and references) and api.response references api.example relationships are indirect in OAS 3.0, since responses reach schemas and examples only through media types or headers, making them transitive shortcuts of the mediatype/header relationships.
The outgoing serves relationship from api.oauthflow to api.operation looks spurious because an OAuth flow is consumed only via its SecurityScheme.
The aggregates and references relationships from api.response to api.schema overlap in meaning.

The associated-with relationship from api.mediatype to api.header is indirect (it goes via Encoding) and therefore redundant.
The relationships from oauthflow, parameter, schema and paths to tag have no basis in OpenAPI.
The serves relationship from api.openapidocument to motivation.stakeholder is weak.

The api.info --aggregates--> api.license relationship understates the structural nesting of License inside Info; the containment should be modeled as composition (License nested in Info, composed into OpenAPIDocument) rather than aggregation or loose association.

The relationships api.info aggregates api.contact and api.info aggregates api.license may be better expressed as composes, since Contact and License are nested and document-bound, unless shared contacts or licenses are intended.

The outgoing 'composes api.paths' relationship from api.operation is inverted, since Paths composes operations (via PathItem) rather than the reverse.
The relationship 'api.operation composes api.paths' inverts containment, since paths contain operations via path items.
The relationship api.operation composes api.paths is inverted, because Paths contains PathItems which contain operations.
The 'serves' predicate for api.tag to api.operation is semantically weak because tags provide no behavior.

api.requestbody declares both 'aggregates' and 'composes' relationships to api.mediatype, plus a 'mediatype serves requestbody' relationship, which are redundant and inconsistent.

A path via parameter, header or media type may make both the api.example references-schema and associated-with-operation relationships redundant.

The relationships api.operation realizes motivation.goal and realizes motivation.outcome use the wrong predicate; they should be supports or delivers.

The relationships apm.resource monitors technology.node and technology.systemsoftware use the wrong predicate, since a Resource passively identifies its host or runtime rather than observing it.

The predicate monitors for apm.dashboard to apm.alert does not fit, because the dashboard displays alert state rather than observing a running system; references or associated-with is closer.
